checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: ~8-second vertical video of fictional adult woman addressing camera in a home setting
must.why: 5 s vertical clip; woman is a runner outdoors on a waterfront, only smiles at camera at the end, not a home setting.

must.item: Complete supplied script audible in English without omissions
must.why: Clip is a generic ad with music and tagline; the supplied script is not present visually, and nothing indicates it was spoken.

must.item: Readable captions reproduce the supplied script exactly
must.why: Only caption is 'Fitrack - Track Every Rep.', not the script.

must.item: Presenter visibly speaks rather than staying still
must.why: She runs, checks her watch and smiles; no visible speech.

must.item: Ad does not label presenter as verified or real customer

exact_text.text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.

faults.what: Brand name misspelled on screen as 'Fitrack' (missing T)
Content ignores the required presenter-script format: no script captions, no speech, wrong setting, wrong length (5 s)
Tagline text overlaps the watch/hand and looks semi-transparent in the mid frame; shot changes abruptly, and the woman's appearance shifts between shots
Invented tagline 'Track Every Rep' that the user never supplied

summary: The clip is a 5-second generic runner ad with the brand misspelled as "Fitrack" and an invented tagline, and it has none of the required script, captions, speaking presenter or home setting.
